rationale: iter-1 LPD-style unrolled image_denoiser (K=2, alpha=0.1, +BF tail). Training diverged: DC gradient step R^T(Rz-g) blew up at epoch 5 (loss 0.04 to 0.17) and timed out at epoch 7/8. Issue is the |R^T R| spectral norm is ~N_angles*det_norm >> 1, so alpha=0.1 is far too large. Need to either init alpha << 1e-3 or precondition the gradient. Inspired by Sidky 2022 top teams (ItNet, YM&RH variational network).

iter-2 K=1 LPD + FBP-preconditioning. Training still diverged (loss 0.00078 -> 0.013, alpha climbing 0.52 -> 0.76) and timed out at ~6 min. FBP-preconditioned grad x_k+1=(1-alpha)*z + alpha*x_in is a learnable interp between denoised and input image; the projection round-trip in the loss path destabilises it. Time cost of even K=1 fp+fbp per call is prohibitive (added 2x to runtime). Pivoting iter-3 to pure shared-weight iterated U-Net (no explicit fp/bp in denoiser).

iter-3 shared-weight iterated U-Net K=2 + BF tail (no projections). Training converged cleanly to loss 0.00037 (same plateau as iter-16 baseline). However iter-unet x2 doubles forward-pass cost and the whole job timed out at the slurm wall (8 min) before validation completed. Train_time was 400s. Next: cut epochs 8 -> 6 to fit the budget.

iter-4 iter_unet_bf K=2 epochs=6: training succeeded (253s, loss converged to 0.00037) but validation OOM'd at the BF unfold (4.79 GiB) — same OOM signature as main-agent iter-18 (BF kernel=11). The iterated K=2 U-Net plus BF needs more memory at val_n=100. Next: chunked validation (val_chunk=16).

Shared-weight iterated U-Net K=2 + BF tail (epochs=6 + chunked val=16). val SSIM 0.6568 vs main-agent best 0.6537 (+0.5%), headroom 0.5788 vs 0.576 (+0.5% relative). The same SmallUNet applied 2x in sequence is a cheap iterative refinement: same params (0.466M) as iter-16 baseline, train time 253s (under wall). Iter-14 (unshared K=2 stack) hurt by 1.0% with 2x params, confirming weight-sharing is the key. Inspired by Sidky 2022 §III ItNet's unrolled U-Net iteration.

K=3 shared-weight iterated U-Net + BF (epochs=5 to fit budget). val 0.6515 vs iter-5 best 0.6568 (-0.8%). K=3 is too deep at constant params; the same SmallUNet applied 3x can't carry the inductive bias for a 3-stage refinement. Possible alternative: K=3 with epochs=8 needs ~470s train but val likely improves. Reverting to K=2 / epochs=6.

Re-baseline iter-5's K=2 shared-weight iter U-Net + BF (epochs=6) under FIXED calibration (display_min=0, display_max=0.05, data_range=0.05) — ported from main-agent iter-24 fix. Headroom 0.5745 (down from previously-reported 0.5788, which was inflated by auto-data-range drift). Now comparable to main iter-25 residual stack (0.5807) and spawn-B iter-2 (0.5831). I'm 0.6-0.9% headroom behind; need iterative gains on top of the calibrated baseline.

iter-8 IteratedResidualStack K=2 (port main iter-25 / spawn-B iter-2 6-block c=32 resnet, share weights, K=2). Timed out at 8:11 after only 3 epochs (loss converging nicely at 0.00039). Full-res 6-block resnet x2 is ~2x the compute of K=2 U-Net; doesn't fit 5-min wall. Next: K=2 + n_blocks=4 to shrink the per-pass cost.

iter-9 IterResStack K=2 n_blocks=4: timed out at 8:14, completed 5/6 epochs. K=2 ResStack is more expensive per-call than K=2 SmallUNet because ResStack has no down/upsampling — every block is full-res 512x512 conv. Need to drop n_blocks further or accept fewer epochs.

iter-10 IterResStack K=2 n_blocks=3 (params 0.113M, eff depth 6 blocks). Train completed (401s, loss 0.00038). val 0.2883/headroom 0.5754 — marginal vs iter-7 K=2 UNet (0.5745), well below main iter-25 K=1 6-block resnet (0.5807) and spawn-B iter-2 (0.5831). At this compute envelope, K=1 + bigger model beats K=2 + smaller model: iteration costs us training depth/epochs we can't recover. Next: inference-time K=2 on K=1-trained model.

iter-11 train K=1 / inference K=2 on 6-block c=32 resnet. Hypothesis: cheap test-time iteration of a well-trained denoiser. Reality: val 0.2990 / headroom 0.527 — catastrophic vs main iter-25 K=1 (0.5807). The residual stack predicts noise; iterating it without joint training keeps subtracting residual on the (now nearly clean) image, oversmoothing and creating systematic bias. Inference-time K does NOT generalise without train-time exposure. Single-pass is the right operating point for residual-predicting denoisers.

iter-12 K=1 6-block resnet + BF tail (Wagner). Hypothesis: compose main iter-25 (resnet) with iter-7's BF gain. Reality: val 0.3089 / headroom 0.5685 — worse than main iter-25 (0.5807) by 1.2pp. Train 453s, just inside budget. ResStack+BF doesn't compose well: the resnet's noise-residual prediction is already edge-aware via GroupNorm; BF post-processing oversmooths.

iter-13 K=2 shared U-Net c=20 + BF (params 0.727M vs iter-7's 0.466M, +56%). Hypothesis: bigger U-Net helps with iterative depth. Reality: val 0.3031 / headroom 0.5712 — worse than iter-7 c=16 K=2 (0.5745). Matches main iter-3 finding that c=24 overfit. Extra capacity hurts on 400 random-ellipse phantoms regardless of iteration depth. Will revert to c=16.

iter-14 EMA decay=0.999 + iter-7 baseline (K=2 U-Net + BF). Headroom 0.5637 vs iter-7 0.5745 (-1.1pp). EMA decay=0.999 has half-life ~700 steps; with only 6 epochs * 400 steps = 2400 total, the shadow weights are dominated by early-training (near-init) trajectories and never converge to the final plateau. Loss plateau matched iter-7 (0.00037) and training ran cleanly (348s), so the regression is entirely the EMA swap. Next: try a much lower decay (e.g. 0.99) to give EMA a half-life ~70 steps matching the convergence regime.

iter-15 EMA decay=0.99 (half-life ~70 steps) on iter-7 K=2 U-Net + BF. Headroom 0.5759 vs iter-7 0.5745 (+0.14pp) and vs iter-14 decay=0.999 (0.5637, -1.1pp). The trend confirms the EMA decay needs to be scaled to convergence regime: decay=0.99 averages the final ~200 steps (the plateau), decay=0.999 averages 700+ steps including pre-convergence. Train trajectory identical to iter-14 (deterministic at seed=42); only swap-eval differs. Result improvement (0.14pp) is below the 1% noise floor per program contract, so discard but record. Next: try even lower decay (0.95) or restrict EMA to final epoch.

iter-16 SWA (uniform mean over last 2 epochs final weights, 800 samples) on iter-7 K=2 U-Net + BF. Headroom 0.5762 vs iter-15 EMA decay=0.99 0.5759 (+0.03pp) and vs iter-7 0.5745 (+0.17pp). SWA marginally beats EMA at this budget but both are below the 1pp keep threshold. The cumulative lesson from iter-14/15/16 is that late-trajectory averaging (EMA decay 0.99 or SWA) provides a robust 0.15-0.17pp lift but the magnitude is below noise. Train_time 235s (vs 242s for iter-15) — SWA adds ~10s for 2 epochs.

iter-17 Charbonnier loss (eps=1e-3) + SWA on iter-7 K=2 U-Net + BF. Headroom 0.5686 vs iter-16 (SWA + MSE) 0.5762 (-0.8pp) and vs iter-7 (MSE no avg) 0.5745 (-0.6pp). Charbonnier underperforms because at eps=1e-3 and typical target residuals ~0.005, the loss is in the L1 regime almost everywhere (linear in |diff|), giving HALF the gradient magnitude of MSE near zero. The model never reaches the loss plateau the MSE version does (Charbonnier loss=0.01179 at ep5, still trending; MSE plateaus at 0.00037 by ep5). 6 epochs is insufficient for L1-like loss on this scale. Could test with eps=1e-2 (push back to L2 regime) but Charbonnier appears wrong tool here.
